task: Copyedit this formal partnership reply only if a real language problem needs correction. The sender wants to decline courteously without creating a future commitment or suggesting that the proposal lacks merit. Keep the existing length and return the letter unchanged if it already does that well.
input: Thank you for inviting our association to co-host the autumn workshop. We appreciate the care you have put into the proposal. Our volunteer hours are already committed through the autumn, so we cannot take on the event. This is a limit on our capacity, not a judgment on the project. We wish you well with the arrangements.

facts.text: The fictional association has been invited to co-host an autumn workshop.
The association appreciates the work put into the proposal.
Its volunteer hours are already committed through the autumn.
It cannot co-host because of capacity, not a negative judgment of the project.

forbidden_additions: A promise to co-host later or to provide volunteers, money, or referrals.
A criticism of the proposal or an invented competing event.
A suggestion that the association is still considering this invitation.
preserve: The distinction between capacity and merit.
The already effective formal voice without cosmetic rewriting.
